A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same ISLock/Anchor Token Matching work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-editing evaluations in Table 1, window-size ablations in Table 2, token-perturbation experiments and appendix attention analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative experiments, qualitative editing results and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Anchor Token Matching, the dynamic candidate window and Adaptive Constraint Relaxation remain unchanged in Section 3.3. Both versions use the same token-selection procedure and model-specific implementations.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same five PIE-Bench-derived editing categories on generated images: object replacement, addition, removal, style transfer and attribute modification. The appendix examples introduce no changed task or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Prompt-to-Prompt, Null-text Inversion, Pix2pix-zero, MasaCtrl, PnPInversion, InstructPix2Pix, MGIE, NPM and PnP-AR. Figure 6 also retains its comparator columns; changed citation numbers do not indicate different baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain the generation-to-editing protocol, 512×512 resolution, ten examples per editing category, GPT-4o mini prompt enhancement, hyperparameters and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: The attention and token-perturbation studies, window-size and threshold ablations, and Appendix B attention analyses retain the same experimental evidence. Shortening Section 4.3 does not remove the displayed ablation cases.

E5.justification: Both retain the SSIM perturbation summaries of 0.56 ± 0.02 and 0.08 ± 0.05 and the same seed-control description for NPM. No run-count disclosure, uncertainty procedure or statistical test is added.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2 match. For example, ISLock retains structure distance 31.79 and whole-image/edited-region CLIP similarities 24.19/21.33. The qualitative examples, plotted trends and appendix results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), including the latent-distance definition, window schedule and threshold rule, are mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about training-free AR editing, implicit structural preservation through ATM and competitive editing performance. The shortened conclusion preserves their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 drops the explicit explanation that a window size of one degenerates to NPM and replaces detailed dog-expression and cake-topping failure descriptions with a general summary. The central structure-versus-flexibility interpretation and applicability boundaries remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New acknowledgments identify the Supercomputing Center of Nankai University as providing computation, a limited disclosure of computing provenance. Appendix A's NVIDIA 3090 hardware, implementation details and hyperparameters, and the promised code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to CMSL, a GAN editing/restoration survey, distribution-aware image translation and ControlVideo, while removing CLIPStyler and UniControlNet. These are limited literature substitutions and additions; the work's central positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 updates affiliations, contact information and corresponding-author designations, adds acknowledgments, revises the related-work sentence and condenses the window-size discussion and conclusion. Most prose and the section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The expanded author block and revised prose cause modest text reflow, with the conclusion now fitting entirely on PDF page 8. Printed page numbers disappear. All twelve figures and both tables retain their substantive displays and organization.

improvement.justification: The method, experimental support, numerical results and appendix content remain unchanged. Shorter prose and updated references and acknowledgments provide limited editorial benefits, while the window-size discussion loses one explicit explanation. These small tradeoffs leave the paper's overall scientific quality and reproducibility essentially unchanged.
